claim: Let \(A,C\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be real symmetric commuting matrices with \(C\succ0\), and consider intermittent dynamics \(\dot x=-Cx\) for a fixed pulse of length \(\epsilon>0\), followed by \(\dot x=Ax\) while the input is zero. Use \(V(x)=\|x\|_2^2\) and trigger the next pulse at the first post-pulse time satisfying \(V(x(t))=V(x(t_k))e^{-\lambda(t-t_k)}\), where \(0<\lambda<2\lambda_{\min}(C)\). If \(a_i,c_i\) are the eigenvalues in a common orthonormal eigenbasis, the exact infimum of the zero-input gap over all nonzero states is \(d_*=\epsilon\min_{i:\,2a_i+\lambda>0}(2c_i-\lambda)/(2a_i+\lambda)\). If the index set is empty, or a given state is supported only on modes with \(2a_i+\lambda\le0\), no finite next trigger occurs. When the set is nonempty, equality is attained exactly by states supported on the minimizing common eigenmodes, so mixing modes cannot shorten the gap.

correctness.rationale: In a common orthonormal eigenbasis, the trigger equality is \(G(d)=\sum_i p_i\exp(-(2c_i-\lambda)\epsilon+(2a_i+\lambda)d)=1\). Before \(d_*\), every exponential factor is below one, while a minimizing pure mode reaches one exactly at \(d_*\). If every coefficient \(2a_i+\lambda\) is nonpositive, every factor stays below one for all finite \(d\). The analytic proof covers all weights and both cases; the script is only a numerical consistency check.

value.rationale: The minimum zero-input duration is a natural actuator-scheduling invariant for intermittent or power-packet control. The formula identifies the worst mode, proves mixtures cannot produce a shorter gap, classifies the no-trigger case, and yields a sharp bound at least twice the generic published lower bound in this class. This supports duty-cycle selection without claiming a general new stability theorem.
